# bcr32

> Unofficial documentation and tools for the Behringer BCR32 MIDI controller and 4-track, 32-step sequencer. Not affiliated with Behringer or Music Tribe. Reference only: no warranty, no claim of accuracy, use at your own risk ([disclaimer](DISCLAIMER.md)).

Control IDs used across the docs: B<n> = button, E<n> = encoder, SEL = select encoder, J<n> = rear jack. Step k = encoder E(24+k).

## Reference

- [BCR32 manual](docs/manual/README.md): every control, mode, menu, value range and procedure, plus known errors in the official manual
- [List of figures](docs/manual/figures.md): numbered drawings of the panel and its controls, with the chapter of each
- [Known issues](docs/manual/15-known-issues.md): faults and limits of the unit and the editor, with source, firmware and status
- [MIDI implementation](docs/manual/16-midi-implementation.md): what the unit sends and accepts on USB, seen on firmware 1.0.3, with the tests that gave no result
- [Full manual in one file](llms-full.txt): `llms.txt` and every manual chapter joined, generated

## Guides

- [Connect to Ableton Live](docs/guides/connect-to-ableton-live.md): USB-MIDI setup, track routing, clock master choice (unverified)
- [How-to guides](docs/guides/README.md): enter a pattern, save and chain, back up, assign controls, encoder modes and rings, DAW mapping, presets as text, drums, scale and transpose, sync, routing, CV and gate
- [Official sources and support](docs/guides/official-sources-and-support.md): official Behringer product page, manual, Control Tribe, Music Tribe's open-source BCR32 repository, support routes, and what to prepare before you ask (draft)
- [Troubleshooting](docs/guides/troubleshooting.md): symptoms and fixes (unverified)
- [Recovery runbook](docs/guides/recovery-runbook.md): recovery steps from least to most invasive, with the unknowns (unverified)
- [Unit session findings](docs/reference/capture-findings.md): results of the first unit session on firmware 1.0.3, MIDI facts seen, open items (draft)
- [BCL preset text format](docs/reference/bcl-preset-text-format.md): preset file syntax for Control Tribe import, with verified and unverified line forms (draft)
- [SysEx dump format](docs/reference/sysex-dump-format.md): byte layout of the All Presets export file (draft)
- [Unit session script](docs/guides/unit-session-script.md): ordered tier 0 tests for the first session at a real unit, with a photo shot list and stop conditions (unverified)

<!-- file: docs/manual/00-how-to-read-this-manual.md -->

# 0. How to read this manual

> **Warning:** This manual is a reference guide only. It can be wrong or out of date. Use it at your own risk. Back up your [presets](13-glossary.md#preset) before you try any procedure. See the [disclaimer](../../DISCLAIMER.md).

- **[Control IDs](13-glossary.md#control-id)** use the official manual's [callout](13-glossary.md#callout) numbers: `B<n>` (button), `E<n>` ([encoder](13-glossary.md#encoder)), `SEL` ([select encoder](13-glossary.md#select-encoder-sel), 58), `DISP` ([display](13-glossary.md#display-disp), 57), `J<n>` (rear jack).
- **[Step](13-glossary.md#step) to encoder:** step k is `E(24+k)`. Step 1 is E25, step 32 is E56. "The nth encoder" in the official manual means E(24+n).
- **Panel label to ID:** the small number printed above each of the 16 parameter buttons (1–16) is not the ID. ID = label + 4, so panel "1 PITCH" is B5 and panel "16 DIRECTION" is B20.
- **Action notation:** `hold X + Y` means keep X down, then press or turn Y. `X ×3s` means hold X for three seconds. `turn E` and `push E` mean rotate and press an encoder. CW and CCW mean clockwise and counter-clockwise.
- **Mode first:** most controls change meaning with the mode, so each procedure starts by naming the mode ([Modes and menus](02-modes-and-menus.md#2-modes-and-menus-state-machine)).
- **New to the unit:** start with the [quick start](10-quick-lookup-how-do-i.md#101-quick-start-play-a-pattern-in-zaq-mode) in chapter 10.

---

<!-- file: docs/manual/01-what-the-unit-is.md -->

# 1. What the unit is

One box with two separate devices. B1 switches between them.

| Device | Name on unit | Button colour | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Sequencer | ZAQ / ZQR / Zaquencer | pink | 4 [tracks](13-glossary.md#track) × 32 [steps](13-glossary.md#step); MIDI, [USB-MIDI](13-glossary.md#usb-midi) and [CV](13-glossary.md#cv)/[gate](13-glossary.md#gate) out |
| Controller | CTRL | amber | 32 [encoders](13-glossary.md#encoder) + 24 buttons sending user-assigned MIDI |
| Settings menus | — | blue | global, sequencer and controller settings |

Key numbers:

- **Sequencer:** 4 tracks, 32 steps, 16 [drum voices](13-glossary.md#drum-voice) per [drum track](13-glossary.md#drum-track), 12 [pattern](13-glossary.md#pattern) [pages](13-glossary.md#page) × 16 [slots](13-glossary.md#slot), [BPM](13-glossary.md#bpm) 30–300.
- **Controller:** 64 [presets](13-glossary.md#preset).
- **Outputs:** 4 CV (0 to +10 V, 1 V/oct) and 4 gate (5 V or 10 V).
- **Notes:** MIDI note range C2–G8 for pitch steps.

---

<!-- file: docs/manual/02-modes-and-menus.md -->

# 2. Modes and menus (state machine)

| Mode / menu | Enter | Exit | Lit buttons |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ZAQ (sequencer) | tap B1 until pink | tap B1 | B1 + used B5–B20 pink |
| CTRL (controller) | tap B1 until amber | tap B1 | amber |
| [Global Settings](13-glossary.md#global-settings) | `B1 ×3s` (either mode) | tap B1 | B1, B5–B12 blue |
| [ZAQ Settings](13-glossary.md#zaq-settings) | in ZAQ: `hold B59 + B61` | B60 (to the [ZAQ Global page](13-glossary.md#zaq-global-page); unverified) | B5–B8 blue |
| [CTRL Settings](13-glossary.md#ctrl-settings) | in CTRL: `hold B59 + B61` | B60 | B5–B6 blue |
| ZAQ Global page | in ZAQ: press B59 | B60 | [encoders](13-glossary.md#encoder) = global params (§6) |
| ZAQ [Mixer](13-glossary.md#mixer) | in ZAQ, sequencer stopped: press B66 | B66 / B60 | B21–24, B5–20 green/red |
| [Real-time record](13-glossary.md#real-time-record) | in ZAQ: press B65 | press B65 | — |
| CTRL Edit | in CTRL: `hold B59 + turn/push E` or `+ press B` | B60 | — |
| CTRL [Learn](13-glossary.md#learn) | in CTRL: `hold B62 + press/turn control` | B60 | — |
| Erase / [SysEx](13-glossary.md#sysex) | `B61`, then `hold SEL + push E…` (§9) | B60 | — |

Power-up mode is set in Global Settings → B5 (DEVICE MODE).

---

<!-- file: docs/manual/03-top-panel-control-map.md -->

# 3. Top panel — control map

Layout is a grid. Coordinates `(row, col)` are for diagram use; row 0 is the top.

## 3.1 Left block: parameter buttons (B5–B20)

<a id="fig-3-3"></a>
<picture>
  <source media="(prefers-color-scheme: dark)" srcset="../assets/figures/fig-3-3-parameter-buttons-dark.png">
  <img src="../assets/figures/fig-3-3-parameter-buttons-light.png" alt="Two rows of eight parameter buttons, B5 to B12 above B13 to B20." width="100%">
</picture>

**Figure 3-3.** Parameter buttons B5 to B20 and the mode button B1. [List of figures](figures.md)

| ID | Panel no. | Label | Pos | ZAQ meaning (§5) | [Global Settings](13-glossary.md#global-settings) | [ZAQ Settings](13-glossary.md#zaq-settings) | [CTRL Settings](13-glossary.md#ctrl-settings) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| B5 | 1 | PITCH | (0,0) | Note pitch per [step](13-glossary.md#step) | Device mode | [Gate](13-glossary.md#gate) out 5/10 V | Output routing |
| B6 | 2 | VELOCITY | (0,1) | Velocity | Device ID | Sync in clock | [MIDI thru](13-glossary.md#midi-thru) |
| B7 | 3 | MUTE | (0,2) | Step mute | [Operation mode](13-glossary.md#operation-mode) | Sync out clock | — |
| B8 | 4 | DELAY | (0,3) | Micro-timing −5…+5 | CV1 measure (calibration) | Sync in start | — |
| B9 | 5 | LENGTH | (0,4) | Note length | [Footswitch](13-glossary.md#footswitch) 1 | — | — |
| B10 | 6 | MIDI CTRL α | (0,5) | α [control lane](13-glossary.md#control-lane) | Footswitch 2 | — | — |
| B11 | 7 | MIDI CTRL β | (0,6) | β control lane | [Firmware](13-glossary.md#firmware) version | — | — |
| B12 | 8 | WAVE GEN | (0,7) | [Wave generator](13-glossary.md#wave-generator) | [Factory restore](13-glossary.md#factory-restore) | — | — |
| B13 | 9 | [CHORD](13-glossary.md#chord) | (1,0) | Chord per step | — | — | — |
| B14 | 10 | STEP SKIP | (1,1) | Skip per step | — | — | — |
| B15 | 11 | SEQ START | (1,2) | Start step | — | — | — |
| B16 | 12 | SEQ LENGTH | (1,3) | Length 1–32 | — | — | — |
| B17 | 13 | SEQ OFFSET | (1,4) | Offset 0–31 | — | — | — |
| B18 | 14 | CLK DIVIDER | (1,5) | Clock division | — | — | — |
| B19 | 15 | [SHUFFLE](13-glossary.md#shuffle) | (1,6) | Shuffle | — | — | — |
| B20 | 16 | DIRECTION | (1,7) | Play direction | — | — | — |

Other roles of B5–B20:

- **[Drum voices](13-glossary.md#drum-voice):** on a [drum track](13-glossary.md#drum-track), B5–B20 = drum voices 1–16.
- **[Pattern](13-glossary.md#pattern) [slots](13-glossary.md#slot):** in STORE / LOAD, B5–B20 = slots 1–16 of the current [page](13-glossary.md#page). Green = slot used. Flashing = current pattern.
- **Virtual keyboard (real-time note entry):** piano layout. Black keys = B6, B7, B9, B10, B11 (C#, D#, F#, G#, A#). White keys = B13–B20 (C, D, E, F, G, A, B, C). B5, B8, B12 not used. Key-to-note mapping is inferred from the layout; the source only lists the buttons.
- **Number pad ([CV](13-glossary.md#cv) calibration):** B5–B14 = digits, B15 = +, B16 = −, B19 = clear, B20 = backspace. The source does not say which button is which digit.
- **[CTRL mode](13-glossary.md#ctrl-mode):** B5–B24 are assignable.

## 3.2 Track buttons and status LEDs

| ID | Label | Pos | Function |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| B1 | ZQR/CTRL | above B12 | Mode toggle; `×3s` = Global Settings |
| B21 | T1 | (0,8) | Select [track](13-glossary.md#track) 1 |
| B22 | T2 | (0,9) | Select track 2 |
| B23 | T3 | (1,8) | Select track 3 |
| B24 | T4 | (1,9) | Select track 4 |
| L2 | MIDI IN / A / B | top right | MIDI activity |
| L3 | FOOTSW 1 / 2 | top right | Flash on footswitch use |
| L4 | USB MODE | top right | USB activity |

Track buttons: current track flashes; green = playing, red = muted in [mixer](13-glossary.md#mixer). Only one track is selected for editing. A small "DRUM NOTES" legend sits between the T rows.

## 3.3 Encoder grid (E25–E56)

<a id="fig-3-4"></a>
<picture>
  <source media="(prefers-color-scheme: dark)" srcset="../assets/figures/fig-3-4-knob-grid-dark.png">
  <img src="../assets/figures/fig-3-4-knob-grid-light.png" alt="Four rows of eight knobs. A number from 1 to 32 is printed above each knob." width="100%">
</picture>

**Figure 3-4.** Knob grid E25 to E56 with the printed numbers 1 to 32. [List of figures](figures.md)

Each [encoder](13-glossary.md#encoder): push switch + LED ring. The step number (1–32) is printed above it. Steps 1, 5, 9 … 29 are boxed as beat markers. The label printed below is its ZAQ Global function (§6).

| Row | Encoders | Steps | Labels below (ZAQ Global) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 2 | E25–E32 | 1–8 | [BPM](13-glossary.md#bpm) · CLOCK INT/EXT · CLOCK OUT · MIDI THROUGH · NOTE [DISPLAY](13-glossary.md#display-disp) · [SCALE](13-glossary.md#scale) · SCALE BASE · [TRANSPOSE](13-glossary.md#transpose) ENBL |
| 3 | E33–E40 | 9–16 | WAVE/TRIG ENBL · GAIN/TRIG [CC](13-glossary.md#control-change-cc) NR · RATE/QUANT · OFFSET/Q-MIXER · TRACKMODE T1 · T2 · T3 · T4 |
| 4 | E41–E48 | 17–24 | MIDI OUT UAB T1 · MIDI OUT CH T1 · UAB T2 · CH T2 · UAB T3 · CH T3 · UAB T4 · CH T4 |
| 5 | E49–E56 | 25–32 | MIDI CTRL α T1 · β T1 · α T2 · β T2 · α T3 · β T3 · α T4 · β T4 |

Row 3 split labels: the first half (WAVE, GAIN, RATE, OFFSET) is the Wave Gen parameter while B12 is held. The second half is the Global function. "UAB" = USB / MIDI A / MIDI B routing.

## 3.4 Right block

| ID | Label | Pos (row, col in block) | ZAQ | CTRL |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| DISP | display | (0,0) | parameter/value | parameter/value |
| [SEL](13-glossary.md#select-encoder-sel) (58) | SELECT | (0,1) | turn = value, push = enter/confirm | same |
| B59 | EDIT / GLOBAL | (1,0) | Global page; hold + encoder = edit all steps | hold = assign controls |
| B60 | EXIT | (1,1) | leave STORE/LOAD/GLOBAL | leave EDIT/STORE/LOAD |
| B61 | STORE | (2,0) | store pattern | store [preset](13-glossary.md#preset) |
| B62 | LD/LRN | (2,1) | LOAD pattern | [LEARN](13-glossary.md#learn) |
| B63 | TAP DELETE / ◄ | (3,0) | erase in real-time rec; page down; hold = peek global value | previous preset/location; previous setup option |
| B64 | TAP WRITE / ► / NOTE RPT | (3,1) | rec sub-mode; page up; in Mixer = [note repeat](13-glossary.md#note-repeat) | next preset/location; next setup option |
| B65 | INST SEL | (4,0) | real-time programming on/off | assignable |
| B66 | MIXER | (4,1) | mixer | assignable |
| B67 | RESET (↻) | (5,0) | jump to step 1 | assignable |
| B68 | PLAY/STOP | (5,1) | start/stop | assignable |

The label "◄ PAGES/PRESETS ►" sits above B63/B64.

**Figure 3-1.** The BCR32 top panel with PITCH selected. [List of figures](figures.md)

<a id="fig-3-2"></a>

**Figure 3-2.** Top panel with the ID of every control. [List of figures](figures.md)

This is our own drawing of the top panel, seen from above. Each cell is a [control ID](13-glossary.md#control-id). The number in a control ID is its [callout](13-glossary.md#callout) number, except for the LEDs: L2 has three LEDs, L3 has two and L4 has one. The drawing shows order and grouping. It does not show true sizes or spacing.

```text
                             B1                   L2.in L2.a L2.b L3.1 L3.2 L4

 B5  B6  B7  B8  B9  B10 B11 B12                  B21  B22
 B13 B14 B15 B16 B17 B18 B19 B20                  B23  B24

 E25 E26 E27 E28 E29 E30 E31 E32                  DISP SEL
 E33 E34 E35 E36 E37 E38 E39 E40                  B59  B60
 E41 E42 E43 E44 E45 E46 E47 E48                  B61  B62
 E49 E50 E51 E52 E53 E54 E55 E56                  B63  B64
                                                  B65  B66
                                                  B67  B68
```

| Area | Controls | Details |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Parameter buttons | `B5`–`B20` | two rows of eight, section 3.1 |
| Mode button | `B1` | above the parameter buttons, at the right, section 3.2 |
| Status LEDs | `L2.in`, `L2.a`, `L2.b`, `L3.1`, `L3.2`, `L4` | top right, section 3.2 |
| Track buttons | `B21`–`B24` | two rows of two, section 3.2 |
| Encoder grid | `E25`–`E56` | four rows of eight, section 3.3 |
| Right block | `DISP`, `SEL`, `B59`–`B68` | six rows of two, section 3.4 |

A photo of the top panel from the unit session on firmware 1.0.3 shows this order (see the [findings](../reference/capture-findings.md#results)). The photos stay local.

<!-- file: docs/manual/04-rear-panel.md -->

# 4. Rear panel

Left to right as seen from behind:

| ID | Jack | Type | Use |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| J69 | POWER | USB-C | power only |
| J70 | POWER/DATA | USB-C | power + [USB-MIDI](13-glossary.md#usb-midi) to computer |
| J71 | MIDI IN | 5-pin DIN | MIDI + clock in |
| J72 | MIDI OUT A | 5-pin DIN | MIDI + clock out |
| J73 | OUT B / THRU | 5-pin DIN | second out, or thru (mirrors MIDI IN + USB) |
| J74, J75 | [FOOTSWITCH](13-glossary.md#footswitch) 1, 2 | 6.35 mm TS | assignable footswitches |
| J76 | SYNC IN | 3.5 mm TRS | tip = clock, ring = start/stop |
| J77 | SYNC OUT | 3.5 mm TRS | clock + start/stop out |
| J78, J80, J82, J84 | [CV](13-glossary.md#cv) 1–4 | 3.5 mm TS | 1 V/oct pitch, [tracks](13-glossary.md#track) 1–4 |
| J79, J81, J83, J85 | [GATE](13-glossary.md#gate) 1–4 | 3.5 mm TS | gate, tracks 1–4 |

Physical order of the output jacks: CV1, GATE1, CV2, GATE2, CV3, GATE3, CV4, GATE4.

Hook-up examples in the source:

- **Studio:** J70 → computer USB. Computer → audio interface → monitors / headphones.
- **Band:** J72 MIDI OUT → synth MIDI IN. J77 SYNC OUT → drum machine SYNC IN. GATE out → second synth GATE IN. Footswitch on J74. USB-C power adapter on J69.

## 4.1 Diagram of the rear panel

This is our own drawing of the rear panel, left to right as seen from behind. Each cell is a [control ID](13-glossary.md#control-id). Gaps separate the groups.

```text
 J69  J70    J71  J72  J73    J74  J75    J76  J77    J78 J79 J80 J81 J82 J83 J84 J85
 PWR  PWR/   IN   OUT  OUT    FS1  FS2    SYN  SYN    CV1 GT1 CV2 GT2 CV3 GT3 CV4 GT4
      DATA        A    B/THRU               IN   OUT
```

| Group | Controls |
| --- | --- |
| Power and USB | `J69`, `J70` |
| MIDI DIN | `J71`, `J72`, `J73` |
| Footswitch | `J74`, `J75` |
| Sync | `J76`, `J77` |
| CV and gate | `J78`–`J85`, in the order CV1, GATE1 to CV4, GATE4 |

---

<!-- file: docs/manual/05-sequencer-per-track-parameters.md -->

# 5. Sequencer (ZAQ mode) — per-track parameters

Select the [track](13-glossary.md#track) first (B21–B24). B5–B20 settings are per track. Everything can change while playing.

General rule: press a parameter button, then turn the [step](13-glossary.md#step) [encoders](13-glossary.md#encoder) E25–E56. `hold B59 + turn any E` moves every step together to its max or min (official manual). Verified on [firmware](13-glossary.md#firmware) 1.0.3: B59 opens the [ZAQ Global page](13-glossary.md#zaq-global-page) instead. Holding a parameter button, for example LENGTH (B9), and turning one knob changed all 32 steps. See [source errors and gaps](12-source-errors-and-gaps.md#12-source-errors-and-gaps).

| Button | Encoders do | Range / options | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| B5 PITCH | note per step | C2–G8; [CV](13-glossary.md#cv) 0–10 V. Ring shows pitch (range set by Global E29); last 3 LEDs show [playhead](13-glossary.md#playhead) | C3 (MIDI 60) |
| B6 VELOCITY | velocity per step | 0–127 | 100 |
| B7 MUTE | toggle play/mute | LED lit = plays | play |
| B8 DELAY | timing shift | −5 (early) … 0 … +5 (late) | 0 |
| B9 LENGTH | note length | 96, t32, 32, t16, 16, t8, 8, t4, 4, t2, 2, t1b, 1b, t2b, 2b, 4b | 32 (32nd note) |
| B10 MIDI CTRL α | α value per step | Off, 1–127; target set by E49/51/53/55 | — |
| B11 MIDI CTRL β | β value per step | Off, 1–127; target set by E50/52/54/56 | — |
| B12 WAVE GEN | hold B12 + E33–E36 | E33 waveform (random, sine, triangle, saw, ramp, rectangle); E34 gain 0–100 (50); E35 rate 1–32 (5); E36 offset 0–127 or "add" (63) | — |
| B13 [CHORD](13-glossary.md#chord) | chord per step (MIDI only) | see list below | Off |
| B14 STEP SKIP | toggle play/skip | LED lit = plays | play |
| B15 SEQ START | turn the encoder of the start step | step 1–32 | 1 |
| B16 SEQ LENGTH | E25 = 1 … E56 = 32 | 1–32 | 32 |
| B17 SEQ OFFSET | E25 = 0 … E56 = 31 | 0–31 steps | 0 |
| B18 CLK DIVIDER | [SEL](13-glossary.md#select-encoder-sel) | 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 24, 12, 6, 3 | 16 |
| B19 [SHUFFLE](13-glossary.md#shuffle) | E30 even, E31 odd | E 0/16/33/50/66/83; O 0/16/33/60/66/83 | 0 |
| B20 DIRECTION | SEL | Forward, Backward, Pip 0 (pendulum, ends repeated), Random, Pendulum | Forward |

Apply Wave Gen to lanes: `hold B12 + press` one or more of B5–B11 (pitch, velocity, mute, delay, length, α, β).

Chord types: Off, Minor, Major, Diminished, Augmented, Diminished 7th, Minor 7th ♭5, Minor 7th, Minor maj7, Major 7th ♭5, Major 7, Major 7 ♯5. The manual prints the entry as one line: "Major 7th with flat 5th, 6th, 7th". Each type also has Octave − and Octave +. Intervals: minor 2nd, major 2nd, minor 3rd, major 3rd, perfect 4th, diminished 5th, perfect 5th, minor 6th, major 6th, minor 7th, major 7th.

---

<!-- file: docs/manual/06-zaq-global-page.md -->

# 6. ZAQ Global page (press B59 in ZAQ)

`hold B63 + turn E` shows a value without changing it.

| Enc | Parameter | Options | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| E25 | [BPM](13-glossary.md#bpm) | 30–300 (internal clock) | — |
| E26 | [Clock source](13-glossary.md#clock-source) | Internal, MIDI, USB, Sync (analog) — limited by [Operation Mode](13-glossary.md#operation-mode) | — |
| E27 | Clock out | outputs that get the clock when the internal clock is the source: Off, MIDI A, MIDI B, A&B, USB, A&USB, B&USB, A&B&USB | Off |
| E28 | [MIDI thru](13-glossary.md#midi-thru) | source Off/MIDI/USB; push [SEL](13-glossary.md#select-encoder-sel) to switch to destination; dest Off, the 7 routings, or the 7 routings Filtered ("F", drops duplicated internal MIDI such as clock). With source Off, Off is the only destination. The full range needs MIXED | — |
| E29 | Note [display](13-glossary.md#display-disp) | OcMi (MIDI no. 1–127, ring = 1 oct), OCNa (octave −2 to +8 and name C to B, ring = 1 oct), AlMi (MIDI no. 1–127, ring = full range), AlNa (octave and name, ring = full range) | — |
| E30 | [Scale](13-glossary.md#scale) | OFF, Major, Minor, Dorian, Phrygian, Lydian, Mixolydian, Locrian, Whole Tone, Minor 7th, Diminished 7th, Octatonic W-H, Octatonic H-W, Major Pentatonic, Minor Pentatonic, Inverted, USER | OFF |
| E31 | Scale base | C–B | — |
| E32 | [Transpose](13-glossary.md#transpose) enable | Off; MIDI ch 1–16; [Track](13-glossary.md#track) (each track follows notes on its own channel); 1-4 … 13-16 (track 1 follows ch n, track 2 ch n+1 …) | Off |
| E33 | Trigger enable | Off or MIDI ch 1–16 for [CC](13-glossary.md#control-change-cc) [pattern](13-glossary.md#pattern) switching | — |
| E34 | Trigger CC no. | CC used to switch patterns | — |
| E35 | Rate / [quantize](13-glossary.md#quantize) | 96, t32, 32, t16 … 4b | 32 |
| E36 | Q on/off | quantize on/off | on |
| E37–E40 | Track mode T1–T4 | [Chord](13-glossary.md#chord) or Drum | Chord (inferred: the manual gives no default) |
| E41/43/45/47 | MIDI out T1–T4 | USB, MIDI A, MIDI B, A&B, USB&A, USB&B, USB&A&B (full list needs MIXED) | — |
| E42/44/46/48 | MIDI channel T1–T4 | 1–16 | — |
| E49/51/53/55 | α target T1–T4 | off, delay, ratchet, [program change](13-glossary.md#program-change-pc), [aftertouch](13-glossary.md#aftertouch-at), [pitch bend](13-glossary.md#pitch-bend-pb), CC 0–127 | off |
| E50/52/54/56 | β target T1–T4 | same as α | off |

Scale notes:

- **Non-destructive:** scale and base bend the notes at playback; the stored notes stay as they are.
- **Make permanent:** press B10 + B11 together. This rewrites the notes and cannot be undone.
- **User scale:** with SCALE (E30) active, `hold B10`. E41–E52 light up; set the 12 notes.

Verified on [firmware](13-glossary.md#firmware) 1.0.3 (2026-11-13, USB operation mode). The option lists are shorter in USB mode.

- **E26 clock source:** two values. INT shows a BPM number. EXT USB IN waits for USB clock.
- **E27 clock out:** two values, OFF and U.
- **E28 MIDI thru:** the source has OFF, MIDI and USB. The display shows the destination and the source together, for example "D:OFF THRU SRC MIDI".
- **E32 transpose enable:** 31 values. OFF, CH 1 to CH 16, TRACK, then the overlapping windows 1-4 to 13-16.
- **E33:** the display shows "PAT.N CH" (pattern change channel).
- **E37 to E40:** the display shows "POLY MODE" with CHORD or DRUM. Track 1 showed DRUM.
- **E41 MIDI out:** three values, U, AB IN and IN.
- **E42 MIDI channel:** CH 2 was set on our unit.

See the [guide to ports, channels and routing](../guides/set-midi-ports-channels-and-routing.md).

---

<!-- file: docs/manual/07-sequencer-procedures.md -->

# 7. Sequencer procedures

## 7.1 Prepare

1. Select [track](13-glossary.md#track) (B21–B24). Confirm track mode is [Chord](13-glossary.md#chord) (Global E37–E40).
2. All [steps](13-glossary.md#step) default to C3. Use that note to tune the synth (warm analog gear up first).
3. `hold B5 + turn any E` to move the default pitch to the key's root note.
4. Press B7 and mute steps you will not use.

## 7.2 Step-enter notes

1. Select track. Press B5.
2. Turn the [encoder](13-glossary.md#encoder) for each step. [DISP](13-glossary.md#display-disp) shows the note.
3. Optional: press B13 and pick a chord per step.

## 7.3 Real-time record (note track)

1. Press B65. DISP shows NOTE (play notes, no recording).
2. Press B64 to cycle NOTE → MONITOR → RECORD → NOTE.
   - **MONITOR:** [pattern](13-glossary.md#pattern) plays (B68), you play along, nothing records.
   - **RECORD:** with [playhead](13-glossary.md#playhead) running, each key press or incoming MIDI note goes to the nearest step.
3. Play from the virtual keyboard (§3.1) or a MIDI keyboard.
4. Erase: in RECORD, `hold B63 + press the note key` while the playhead passes the steps. Hold for a full pattern to erase every instance.
5. Press B65 to leave.

## 7.4 Drum tracks

- **Set a track to Drum:** B59 (Global), turn E37–E40 for the track to Drum.
- **[Drum voice](13-glossary.md#drum-voice) pitches:** in Global, `hold track button (B21–24)`; E25–E40 set voices 1–16. DISP and ring show the note; the note also sounds on the track's outputs.
- **Step-enter:** B65, press drum B5–B20, turn the encoders of the steps you want. Turn again to remove. [Ring LED](13-glossary.md#ring-led) marks programmed steps.
- **Fill all steps:** `hold drum button + turn any E CW`. Clear all: same, CCW.
- **Random:** select drum (B5–B20), `hold B65 + press B12`. Remove single steps by turning CCW.
- **Real-time:** B65, then B64 toggles MONITOR / RECORD. Erase with `hold B63 + drum button`.

## 7.5 Mixer and note repeat

1. Stop the sequencer. Press B66.
2. B21–B24 mute tracks; B5–B20 mute drum voices. Green = on, red = muted.
3. [Note repeat](13-glossary.md#note-repeat): `hold B64 + turn any E` for rate (96, t32, 32, t16, 16, t8, 8, t4, 4). Still holding B64, press a track button (whole track) or a drum button (one voice).

## 7.6 Patterns

- **Store (temporary):** `hold B61`, [page](13-glossary.md#page) with B63/B64 (1–12), press [slot](13-glossary.md#slot) B5–B20. B61 stays lit.
- **Store (permanent):** then press B60, `hold SEL + press B61`. DISP confirms. Without this step the pattern is lost at power-off.
- **Load:** press B62, page with B63/B64, press slot. Press B60. A load while playing switches at the end of the current pattern.
- **Chain:** `hold a pattern button + press another`; patterns play in order. Unverified, from the ZAQ Audio forum: the chain switches when the slowest track has played once, and [quantize](13-glossary.md#quantize) on delays the switch. See the [guide](../guides/save-load-and-chain-patterns.md).
- **No auto-load:** nothing loads at power-up.
- **Copy track:** `hold destination track button + press source track button`.
- **Copy pattern between tracks:** press the pattern button before the source track (source wording unclear).

## 7.7 Transport

B68 play/stop. B67 back to step 1. [Footswitch](13-glossary.md#footswitch) 1 = start/stop, footswitch 2 = next pattern (when set to ZAQ in Global).

---

<!-- file: docs/manual/08-controller.md -->

# 8. Controller (CTRL mode)

Assignable: B5–B24, E25–E56 (turn = continuous, push = on/off), B65–B68, [footswitches](13-glossary.md#footswitch) (when Global B9/B10 = CTRL).

## 8.1 Assign a control

1. `hold B59 + turn/push the encoder` or `+ press the button`.
2. Turn [SEL](13-glossary.md#select-encoder-sel) to pick the type. Types: Off, [PC](13-glossary.md#program-change-pc), [CC](13-glossary.md#control-change-cc), [NRPN](13-glossary.md#nrpn), [PB](13-glossary.md#pitch-bend-pb) ([encoders](13-glossary.md#encoder) only), Note (buttons only), [AT](13-glossary.md#aftertouch-at), GS, [MMC](13-glossary.md#mmc) (buttons only).
3. B63/B64 [step](13-glossary.md#step) through the setup fields; SEL sets each value.
4. B60 to finish.

## 8.2 Learn

`hold B62 + press/turn the control`, then send MIDI from an external device (DIN or USB). Fine-tune afterwards with B59.

## 8.3 Presets

- **Store:** B61, pick location with B63/B64, B61 again to confirm, B61 a third time to write (temporary). Permanent: `hold SEL + press B61`.
- **Load:** B63/B64 to the location; it loads at once.

## 8.4 Setup fields per type

Each message type has its own fields. B63 and B64 step through the fields. SEL sets the value. A dash means the control has no such field. Manual [pages](13-glossary.md#page) 24 to 34.

### 8.4.1 Button and encoder modes

| Mode | Control | Action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Tog On | button | Latch. A press sends the maximum. The next press sends the minimum. |
| Tog Off | button | Momentary. The button sends the maximum while down and the minimum when released. |
| Inc | button | Each press raises the value by the increment, from the minimum to the maximum. |
| Absolute | encoder | 7-bit absolute value. |
| ABS_14 | encoder | 14-bit absolute value (fine control). |
| REL1 | encoder | Minimum for CCW, maximum for CW. |
| REL2 | encoder | 63 for CCW, 65 for CW. |
| REL3 | encoder | 1 for CCW, 65 for CW. |
| R1_14 | encoder | CCW: coarse 0, fine 1. CW: coarse 127, fine 127. |
| R2_14 | encoder | CCW: coarse 63, fine 127. CW: coarse 64, fine 1. |
| R3_14 | encoder | CCW: coarse 64, fine 1. CW: coarse 0, fine 1. |
| INC/DEC | encoder | CW sends increment 1. CCW sends decrement 1. |

### 8.4.2 LED options

<a id="fig-8-1"></a>
<picture>
  <source media="(prefers-color-scheme: dark)" srcset="../assets/figures/fig-8-1-ring-styles-dark.png">
  <img src="../assets/figures/fig-8-1-ring-styles-light.png" alt="Sixteen knob rings. Row 1 shows eight LED styles at half value. Row 2 shows four more styles at half value, then four styles at zero." width="100%">
</picture>

**Figure 8-1.** LED styles around the knobs, at half value and at zero (model, unverified on the unit). [List of figures](figures.md)

The LED options set how the ring around an encoder shows its value. The default is 1dot_in. Manual page 26.

| Style | Ring behaviour |
| --- | --- |
| Off | The ring stays dark. |
| 1dot_in | One LED lights at a time as the encoder moves (default). |
| 1dot_ex | As 1dot_in, but all LEDs are dark at zero. |
| 2dot_in | The LED next to the lit one lights before the first goes out. The side depends on CW or CCW. |
| 2dot_ex | As 2dot_in, but all LEDs are dark at zero. |
| Bar | LEDs light and stay lit for CW. They go out one by one for CCW. |
| Bar− | As Bar, but all LEDs are dark at zero. |
| Sprd | The centre LED is lit at zero. LEDs on both sides light as the value rises. |
| Pan | The manual gives the same text as Sprd. See [Source errors and gaps](12-source-errors-and-gaps.md#12-source-errors-and-gaps). |
| Qual | All LEDs are lit at the minimum. They go out on both sides until only the centre LED stays lit at the maximum. |
| Cut | All LEDs are lit at the minimum. They go out one by one as the value rises. |
| Damp | The rightmost LED is lit at the minimum. The other LEDs light one by one as the value rises. |

### 8.4.3 PC (program control)

| Field | Button | Encoder |
| --- | --- | --- |
| MIDI channel | 1–16 | 1–16 |
| Parameter (bank number) | 0–127 | 0–127 |
| Minimum value | 0–127 | Off, 0–127 |
| Maximum value | 0–127 | 0–127 |
| Mode | Tog Off, Inc | Absolute |
| LED options | — | the 12 styles |
| [Display](13-glossary.md#display-disp) | On, Off | On, Off |

### 8.4.4 CC (continuous controller)

| Field | Button | Encoder |
| --- | --- | --- |
| MIDI channel | 1–16 | 1–16 |
| Parameter (controller) | 0–127 | Off, 0–127 |
| Minimum value | 0–127 | 0–127 |
| Maximum value | 0–127 | 0–127 |
| Mode | Tog On, Tog Off, Inc | Absolute, A14, REL1, REL2, REL3, R1_14, R2_14, R3_14 |
| Increment options | −127 to +127 | — |
| LED options | — | the 12 styles |
| Display | On, Off | On, Off |

### 8.4.5 NRPN

| Field | Button | Encoder |
| --- | --- | --- |
| MIDI channel | 1–16 | 1–16 |
| Parameter (controller) | 0–127 | 0–16383 |
| Minimum value | 0–127 | 0–16383 |
| Maximum value | 0–127 | 0–16383 |
| Mode | Tog On, Tog Off, Inc | Absolute, A14, REL1, REL2, REL3, R1_14, R2_14, R3_14, INC/DEC |
| Increment options | −127 to +127 | — |
| LED options | — | the 12 styles |
| Display | On, Off | On, Off |

### 8.4.6 Note

Buttons only. The manual names the fields "Parameter (controller)" and "Value". Note number and velocity are the likely meanings (unverified).

| Field | Button |
| --- | --- |
| MIDI channel | 1–16 |
| Parameter (controller) | 0–127 |
| Value | 0–127 |
| Mode | Tog On, Tog Off, Inc |
| Display | On, Off |

### 8.4.7 PB (pitch bend)

Encoders only.

| Field | Encoder |
| --- | --- |
| MIDI channel | 1–16 |
| Parameter (controller) | 0–127 |
| Value | 0–127 |
| Mode | Absolute |
| LED options | the 12 styles |
| Display | On, Off |

### 8.4.8 AT (aftertouch)

| Field | Button | Encoder |
| --- | --- | --- |
| MIDI channel | 1–16 | 1–16 |
| Parameter (controller) | All, 0–127 | 0–127 |
| Minimum value | 0–127 | 0–127 |
| Maximum value | 0–127 | 0–127 |
| Mode | — | Absolute |
| Increment options | −127 to +127 (default 1) | — |
| LED options | — | the 12 styles |
| Display | On, Off | On, Off |

### 8.4.9 GS (most used parameters)

Buttons and encoders use one parameter list. The list is: Cutoff, Resonance, Rate, Depth, Delay, Attack, Decay, Release, Modulation, Portamento, Volume, Pan, Reverb, CRS, VAR.

| Field | Button | Encoder |
| --- | --- | --- |
| MIDI channel | 1–16 | 1–16 |
| Parameter | the list above | the list above |
| Minimum value | 0–127 | 0–127 |
| Maximum value | 0–127 | 0–127 |
| Mode | Tog On, Tog Off | Absolute, A14, REL1, REL2, REL3, R1_14, R2_14, R3_14, INC/DEC |
| LED options | — | the 12 styles |
| Display | On, Off | On, Off |

### 8.4.10 MMC (MIDI machine code)

Buttons only.

| Field | Button |
| --- | --- |
| MIDI device ID | 0–126, All |
| Parameter | Play, Pause, Stop, Forward, Rewind, Location, In, Out |
| Start position locate (HH:MM) | 0–127, Off |
| Start position locate (SS:FF) | 0–127, Off |
| Mode | Off, 24, 25, 30, 30d (frames per second) |
| Display | On, Off |

The printed parameter list ends with a comma. It may be cut short. See [Source errors and gaps](12-source-errors-and-gaps.md#12-source-errors-and-gaps).

## 8.5 CTRL Settings (`hold B59 + B61` in CTRL)

- **B5 output routing:** USB, MIDI A, MIDI B, A&B, USB&A, USB&B, USB&A&B.
- **B6 [MIDI thru](13-glossary.md#midi-thru):** source via E28 (Off, MIDI, USB); destination via SEL (Off, 7 routings, or 7 Filtered). Push SEL to save, B60 to exit.
- **B7 echo dead time:** not in the manual. Verified on [firmware](13-glossary.md#firmware) 1.0.3: the display shows `ECHO deadtime 100ms`. The range is not recorded.

> **Note:** Verified on firmware 1.0.3 (2026-11-11): the menu has three items (B5 to B7). The display showed output port `U` (USB), thru destination off and thru source off.

<!-- file: docs/manual/09-global-sync-memory-and-maintenance.md -->

# 9. Global, sync, memory and maintenance

## 9.1 Global Settings (`B1 ×3s`; SEL to change, push SEL to save)

| Btn | Setting | Options |
| --- | --- | --- |
| B5 | Device mode | ZQR or CTRL at power-up |
| B6 | Device ID | 1–255 (unique per unit) |
| B7 | [Operation mode](13-glossary.md#operation-mode) | USB (no [DIN MIDI](13-glossary.md#din-midi), no internal clock; USB + analog sync on); STDL (DIN MIDI, MIDI sync, internal clock; no USB, no analog sync); MIXED (all) |
| B8 | CV1 measure | starts calibration (§9.4) |
| B9 | [Footswitch](13-glossary.md#footswitch) 1 | ZAQ start/stop or CTRL programmable |
| B10 | Footswitch 2 | ZAQ next [pattern](13-glossary.md#pattern) or CTRL programmable |
| B11 | [Firmware](13-glossary.md#firmware) version | [display](13-glossary.md#display-disp) only |
| B12 | [Factory restore](13-glossary.md#factory-restore) | Cancel / OK; takes over a minute |
| B13 | Pattern change channel | not in the manual; `Off` seen on firmware 1.0.3; other values unseen |
| B14 | [Encoder](13-glossary.md#encoder) acceleration | not in the manual; `2` seen on firmware 1.0.3; range unseen |
| B15 | Footswitch polarity | not in the manual; `AUTO` seen on firmware 1.0.3; other values unseen |

> **Note:** Verified on firmware 1.0.3 (2026-11-11): the menu lights B1 and B5–B15 (panel buttons 1–11) in blue, three more than the official manual lists. B11 shows the firmware version (1.0.3). B13 to B15 are the three extra settings above. LED luminosity, which the vendor editor lists, has no button. Read the display before you confirm anything on B12. The unit prints the numbers 1 to 16 above B5 to B20; the ID is the printed number plus 4.

## 9.2 ZAQ Settings (`hold B59 + B61` in ZAQ)

B5 [gate](13-glossary.md#gate) level 5 V / 10 V. B6 sync-in [ppqn](13-glossary.md#ppqn) (1, 2, 4, 24, 48). B7 sync-out ppqn (same). B8 sync-in start: GATE (trigger on ring) or CLOCK (starts when clock on tip). Push [SEL](13-glossary.md#select-encoder-sel) to confirm each choice. B60 exits to the [ZAQ Global page](13-glossary.md#zaq-global-page) (the manual says "exit the menu to the ZAQ GLOBAL menu, and return to the Zaquencer functions"; unverified). Verified on firmware 1.0.3 (2026-11-11): B8 shows `SYN IN STRT` with the value GATE. The value CLOCK was not seen.

## 9.3 Erase and SysEx (all start with B61, then `hold SEL + push E…`)

| Goal | Mode | Sequence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Erase menu | either | B61, `hold SEL + push E49` (source says "25th encoder (50)"; 25th = E49) |
| → reset sequencer globals | ZAQ | push E31, push again to confirm |
| → erase sequences, keep globals | ZAQ | push E32, push again |
| → erase all controller memory | CTRL | push E32, push again |
| [SysEx](13-glossary.md#sysex) export menu | either | B61, `hold SEL + push E25` |
| → all ZAQ memory | ZAQ | push E29 |
| → 12 sequence [pages](13-glossary.md#page) | ZAQ | push E30 |
| → current page | ZAQ | push E31 |
| → current sequence | ZAQ | push E32 |
| → all 64 [presets](13-glossary.md#preset) | CTRL | push E31 |
| → current preset | CTRL | push E32 |
| SysEx import | either | B61, `hold SEL + push E33`; then send SysEx |

B60 returns to normal.

## 9.4 CV calibration (factory-calibrated; only if needed)

Needs a millivolt meter. For [CV](13-glossary.md#cv) output n (1–4):

1. `B1 ×3s`, press B8. DISP shows MIN.
2. Meter on CV n. Turn E(24+n). B5–B14 become a number pad (amber). B15 is + (green), B16 is − (red), B19 clears (blue), B20 is backspace (pink).
3. Turn E(32+n), enter the meter reading.
4. Turn E(40+n), enter the meter reading.
5. Push E(24+n). Turn it CCW: meter reads 0 V. Turn CW: meter reads +10 V.
6. Repeat for the next output. Press B1 to finish.

## 9.5 Control Tribe

The Behringer [Control Tribe](13-glossary.md#control-tribe) app edits most functions and installs firmware updates.

---

<!-- file: docs/manual/10-quick-lookup-how-do-i.md -->

# 10. Quick lookup: "how do I …"

This chapter has two quick starts and a task lookup. Each task links to the chapter that holds the detail.

> **Note:** The [steps](13-glossary.md#step) come from the official manual. They are unverified on a unit unless a line says "verified" with a [firmware](13-glossary.md#firmware) version. Read [Source errors and gaps](12-source-errors-and-gaps.md#12-source-errors-and-gaps) if a step does not give the result shown.

## 10.1 Quick start: play a pattern in ZAQ mode

Goal: enter a short note [pattern](13-glossary.md#pattern) on [track](13-glossary.md#track) 1 and hear it. The steps need a synth that takes [CV](13-glossary.md#cv) and [gate](13-glossary.md#gate), or MIDI.

### Connect the unit

1. Connect J70 (POWER/DATA) to a computer or a USB power supply. The unit starts.
2. Connect the synth. Use one of the two routes in the table.

| Route | Connect | Note |
| --- | --- | --- |
| CV and gate | J78 (CV 1) to the pitch input. J80 (CV 2) is track 2, and so on. J79 (GATE 1) to the gate input | CV is 1 V per octave. Gate is 5 V or 10 V ([ZAQ Settings](09-global-sync-memory-and-maintenance.md#92-zaq-settings-hold-b59--b61-in-zaq)) |
| MIDI | J72 (MIDI OUT A) to the synth MIDI IN | Set the track port and channel in step 6 |

### Enter the notes

1. Tap B1 until the button is pink. The unit is in [ZAQ mode](13-glossary.md#zaq-mode).
2. Press B21 (T1). The track 1 button flashes.
3. Press B5 (PITCH). [DISP](13-glossary.md#display-disp) shows the pitch of a step.
4. Turn E25. DISP shows the note of step 1. All steps start at C3.
5. Turn E26 to E32 for steps 2 to 8. Step k is E(24+k).
6. If you use MIDI, press B59. Turn E41 to pick the port. Turn E42 to pick the channel. Press B60 to leave.
7. Press B7 (MUTE). Toggle each unused step. The LED of a muted step goes dark.
8. Press B68 (PLAY/STOP). The pattern plays. The [playhead](13-glossary.md#playhead) moves on the [ring LEDs](13-glossary.md#ring-led).
9. Press B68 again. The pattern stops.

> **Note:** The manual says "toggle" for mute and skip. It does not say whether to turn or push the [encoder](13-glossary.md#encoder). Test it on the unit.

**Tip:** `hold B5 + turn any E` moves all steps together. Use it to set the key root first.

### Shape the pattern

Press a parameter button, then turn the step encoders. The change takes effect while the pattern plays.

| Press | Turn the encoders to change | Range |
| --- | --- | --- |
| B6 (VELOCITY) | velocity of each step | 0 to 127 |
| B9 (LENGTH) | note length of each step | 96 to 4b |
| B8 (DELAY) | timing of each step | −5 to +5 |
| B16 (SEQ LENGTH) | the last step (E25 is 1, E56 is 32) | 1 to 32 |

Chapter [5](05-sequencer-per-track-parameters.md#5-sequencer-zaq-mode--per-track-parameters) lists all 16 parameters.

### Save the pattern

> **Warning:** The unit loses a pattern at power-off if you do not store it permanently. Nothing loads at power-up.

1. Hold B61 (STORE). [Page](13-glossary.md#page) with B63 and B64 to pick a page from 1 to 12.
2. Press a [slot](13-glossary.md#slot) button from B5 to B20. B61 stays lit.
3. Press B60 (EXIT).
4. Hold [SEL](13-glossary.md#select-encoder-sel) and press B61. DISP confirms the store.

To load the pattern, press B62, page with B63 and B64, press the slot, then press B60. See [Patterns](07-sequencer-procedures.md#76-patterns).

## 10.2 Quick start: send a MIDI control from CTRL mode

Goal: make encoder E25 send a [CC](13-glossary.md#control-change-cc) (control change) message.

1. Tap B1 until the button is amber. The unit is in [CTRL mode](13-glossary.md#ctrl-mode).
2. Hold B59 and turn E25. The unit enters CTRL Edit.
3. Turn SEL to pick CC. The type changes.
4. Press B64 to move to the next field. Turn SEL to set the value. Repeat for each field.
5. Press B60. The setup ends.
6. Turn E25. The unit sends the CC message on the port and channel you set.

[Learn](13-glossary.md#learn) mode is faster if a device can send the message. Hold B62 and turn E25. Then send the message from the other device. See [Learn](08-controller.md#82-learn).

> **Note:** Verified on firmware 1.0.3 (2026-11-11): the first factory [preset](13-glossary.md#preset) sent CC 97, 65, 66 and 98 on channel 1 of the port `BCR-32 CTRL`. Which control sends which message is not mapped yet.

Store the setup in a preset. See [Presets](08-controller.md#83-presets). The field lists for each type are in [Setup fields per type](08-controller.md#84-setup-fields-per-type).

## 10.3 Task lookup

Each row shows the mode, the key sequence and the chapter. The notation is in [How to read this manual](00-how-to-read-this-manual.md#0-how-to-read-this-manual).

### Play and edit the sequencer

| Task | Mode | Keys | Detail |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Switch between sequencer and controller | any | tap B1 | [2](02-modes-and-menus.md#2-modes-and-menus-state-machine) |
| Start or stop the pattern | ZAQ | B68 | [7.7](07-sequencer-procedures.md#77-transport) |
| Go back to step 1 | ZAQ | B67 | [7.7](07-sequencer-procedures.md#77-transport) |
| Change the note of a step | ZAQ | B5, turn the step encoder | [7.2](07-sequencer-procedures.md#72-step-enter-notes) |
| Move all notes together | ZAQ | `hold B5 + turn any E` | [5](05-sequencer-per-track-parameters.md#5-sequencer-zaq-mode--per-track-parameters) |
| Add a [chord](13-glossary.md#chord) to a step | ZAQ | B13, turn the step encoder | [5](05-sequencer-per-track-parameters.md#5-sequencer-zaq-mode--per-track-parameters) |
| Skip a step | ZAQ | B14, toggle the step | [5](05-sequencer-per-track-parameters.md#5-sequencer-zaq-mode--per-track-parameters) |
| Shorten a track to 16 steps | ZAQ | select the track, B16, turn E40 | [5](05-sequencer-per-track-parameters.md#5-sequencer-zaq-mode--per-track-parameters) |
| Change the play direction | ZAQ | B20, turn SEL | [5](05-sequencer-per-track-parameters.md#5-sequencer-zaq-mode--per-track-parameters) |
| Add swing | ZAQ | B19, turn E30 (even steps) or E31 (odd steps) | [5](05-sequencer-per-track-parameters.md#5-sequencer-zaq-mode--per-track-parameters) |
| Make random velocities | ZAQ | `hold B12`, turn E33 to random, then `hold B12 + B6` | [5](05-sequencer-per-track-parameters.md#5-sequencer-zaq-mode--per-track-parameters) |
| Record notes in real time | ZAQ | B65, B64 to RECORD, B68, play the keys | [7.3](07-sequencer-procedures.md#73-real-time-record-note-track) |
| Make a track a [drum track](13-glossary.md#drum-track) | ZAQ | B59, turn E37 to E40 to Drum | [7.4](07-sequencer-procedures.md#74-drum-tracks) |
| Mute a track | ZAQ | stop, B66, press the track button | [7.5](07-sequencer-procedures.md#75-mixer-and-note-repeat) |
| Repeat notes | ZAQ | `hold B64 + turn any E`, then press a track button | [7.5](07-sequencer-procedures.md#75-mixer-and-note-repeat) |
| Copy a track | ZAQ | `hold` the destination track button, press the source | [7.6](07-sequencer-procedures.md#76-patterns) |
| Chain two patterns | ZAQ | `hold` a pattern button, press another | [7.6](07-sequencer-procedures.md#76-patterns) |
| Store a pattern for good | ZAQ | `hold B61`, page, slot, B60, `hold SEL + B61` | [7.6](07-sequencer-procedures.md#76-patterns) |
| Load a pattern | ZAQ | B62, page, slot, B60 | [7.6](07-sequencer-procedures.md#76-patterns) |

### Tempo, clock and routing

| Task | Mode | Keys | Detail |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Change the tempo | ZAQ | B59, turn E25 | [6](06-zaq-global-page.md#6-zaq-global-page-press-b59-in-zaq) |
| Sync to a DAW over USB | ZAQ | B59, E26 to USB. [Operation mode](13-glossary.md#operation-mode) must be USB or MIXED | [6](06-zaq-global-page.md#6-zaq-global-page-press-b59-in-zaq), [9.1](09-global-sync-memory-and-maintenance.md#91-global-settings-b1-3s-sel-to-change-push-sel-to-save) |
| Send clock to MIDI A | ZAQ | B59, E27 to MIDI A. The [clock source](13-glossary.md#clock-source) must be Internal | [6](06-zaq-global-page.md#6-zaq-global-page-press-b59-in-zaq) |
| Set the MIDI channel of a track | ZAQ | B59, turn E42, E44, E46 or E48 | [6](06-zaq-global-page.md#6-zaq-global-page-press-b59-in-zaq) |
| Set the output port of a track | ZAQ | B59, turn E41, E43, E45 or E47 | [6](06-zaq-global-page.md#6-zaq-global-page-press-b59-in-zaq) |
| Lock the notes to a [scale](13-glossary.md#scale) | ZAQ | B59, E30 for the scale, E31 for the root | [6](06-zaq-global-page.md#6-zaq-global-page-press-b59-in-zaq) |
| Set the gate level (5 V or 10 V) | [ZAQ Settings](13-glossary.md#zaq-settings) | `hold B59 + B61`, B5 | [9.2](09-global-sync-memory-and-maintenance.md#92-zaq-settings-hold-b59--b61-in-zaq) |
| Use the sync jacks | ZAQ Settings | `hold B59 + B61`, B6 to B8 | [9.2](09-global-sync-memory-and-maintenance.md#92-zaq-settings-hold-b59--b61-in-zaq) |
| Power the unit from a charger | any | connect J69 | [4](04-rear-panel.md#4-rear-panel) |

### Controller

| Task | Mode | Keys | Detail |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Assign a control | CTRL | `hold B59 + turn E`, turn SEL to the type, B64 for the next field | [8.1](08-controller.md#81-assign-a-control) |
| Learn a control from incoming MIDI | CTRL | `hold B62 + turn E`, send the message | [8.2](08-controller.md#82-learn) |
| Store a preset | CTRL | B61, B63 or B64 for the location, B61, B61 | [8.3](08-controller.md#83-presets) |
| Store a preset for good | CTRL | after the store, `hold SEL + B61` | [8.3](08-controller.md#83-presets) |
| Load a preset | CTRL | B63 or B64 to the location | [8.3](08-controller.md#83-presets) |
| Assign a [footswitch](13-glossary.md#footswitch) | CTRL | [Global Settings](13-glossary.md#global-settings): B9 or B10 to CTRL | [9.1](09-global-sync-memory-and-maintenance.md#91-global-settings-b1-3s-sel-to-change-push-sel-to-save) |

### Settings and maintenance

> **Warning:** B8 in Global Settings starts CV calibration. B12 starts a [factory restore](13-glossary.md#factory-restore). Read the display before you push SEL.

| Task | Mode | Keys | Detail |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Open Global Settings | any | `B1 ×3s` | [9.1](09-global-sync-memory-and-maintenance.md#91-global-settings-b1-3s-sel-to-change-push-sel-to-save) |
| Set the power-up mode | Global Settings | B5, turn SEL, push SEL | [9.1](09-global-sync-memory-and-maintenance.md#91-global-settings-b1-3s-sel-to-change-push-sel-to-save) |
| Read the firmware version | Global Settings | B11 | [9.1](09-global-sync-memory-and-maintenance.md#91-global-settings-b1-3s-sel-to-change-push-sel-to-save) |
| Export all ZAQ memory (backup) | ZAQ | B61, `hold SEL + push E25`, push E29 | [9.3](09-global-sync-memory-and-maintenance.md#93-erase-and-sysex-all-start-with-b61-then-hold-sel--push-e) |
| Erase memory | either | start with B61. The steps destroy data | [9.3](09-global-sync-memory-and-maintenance.md#93-erase-and-sysex-all-start-with-b61-then-hold-sel--push-e) |
| Calibrate the CV outputs | Global Settings | B8. The unit is calibrated at the factory | [9.4](09-global-sync-memory-and-maintenance.md#94-cv-calibration-factory-calibrated-only-if-needed) |
| Recover a unit that does not start | — | see the [recovery runbook](../guides/recovery-runbook.md) | — |
| Fix a connection or sync fault | — | see [troubleshooting](../guides/troubleshooting.md) | — |

<!-- file: docs/manual/11-display-strings-seen-in-the-source.md -->

# 11. Display strings seen in the source

ZQR, CTRL, USB, STDL, MIXED, Cancel, OK, MIN, NOTE, MONITOR, RECORD, OcMi, OCNa, AlMi, AlNa, F (filtered thru), E/O ([shuffle](13-glossary.md#shuffle)), Pip 0. The example [display](13-glossary.md#display-disp) reads "drums RD-8 006".

<!-- file: docs/manual/12-source-errors-and-gaps.md -->

# 12. Source errors and gaps

| Location | Issue | Working assumption |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [ZAQ Settings](13-glossary.md#zaq-settings) B8 | text contains a draft tag "<CHECK?>" | [GATE](13-glossary.md#gate) = start trigger on ring; CLOCK = start on clock. Partly verified on [firmware](13-glossary.md#firmware) 1.0.3: B8 shows `SYN IN STRT` = GATE; CLOCK unseen |
| [CTRL Settings](13-glossary.md#ctrl-settings) + Global E28/E41 | "MIXED is selected using button 7 (Note Mute)" | B7 in [Global Settings](13-glossary.md#global-settings) = [Operation mode](13-glossary.md#operation-mode). Verified on firmware 1.0.3: B7 shows the operation mode (USB). MIXED is unseen |
| Erase | "25th [encoder](13-glossary.md#encoder) (50)" | E49 (all other ordinals in the source map n → E(24+n)) |
| §[ZAQ mode](13-glossary.md#zaq-mode) | NOTE LENGTH values printed inside the [CHORD](13-glossary.md#chord) list | lengths listed in §5 |
| Chord list | one printed line "Major 7th with flat 5th, 6th, 7th" (checked on the [page](13-glossary.md#page) image; the text extract only looks garbled) | possibly three entries; unverified |
| α targets | "CC0– 27" | [CC](13-glossary.md#control-change-cc) 0–127 |
| LOAD | "buttons 63 & 63" | 63 & 64. Verified on firmware 1.0.3: B64 pages up, B63 pages down |
| MIDI out list E41… | garbled with [transpose](13-glossary.md#transpose) list; "Input channel" appears | "Input channel" probably belongs to E32 |
| Copy [pattern](13-glossary.md#pattern) | ordering of presses unclear | test on the unit |
| Pattern chain | does not say which view (LOAD?) | probably LOAD view |
| User [scale](13-glossary.md#scale) | "while in SCALE mode" not defined | while E30 is the active global control |
| Virtual keyboard / number pad | key-to-note and key-to-digit maps not given | piano layout inferred (§3.1). Tested on firmware 1.0.3: the keyboard sent nothing on USB, so no note map was read; open |
| Specifications | no spec page (power draw, size, weight) | unknown |
| Global Settings | manual lists 8 settings (panel buttons 1–8); firmware 1.0.3 lights 11 buttons (1–11) | Resolved on firmware 1.0.3: panel buttons 9 to 11 (B13 to B15) are pattern change channel, encoder acceleration and [footswitch](13-glossary.md#footswitch) polarity. LED luminosity has no button |
| CTRL Settings | manual lists 2 items (B5, B6); firmware 1.0.3 has a third | Verified on firmware 1.0.3: B7 is `ECHO deadtime` (100ms seen). Not in the manual |
| LED options table (p. 26) | Sprd and Pan have the same description; the third column is headed MINIMUM/MAXIMUM and is empty | Sprd and Pan differ in a way the manual does not say; ignore the empty column. Test on the unit |
| Encoder modes | 14-bit absolute is "ABS_14" on p. 24, "A14" on pp. 28 to 32 and "A 14" on p. 32 | one mode; the data uses A14 |
| GS parameter lists | "Attack. Decay" printed with a full stop | two parameters, Attack and Decay |
| [MMC](13-glossary.md#mmc) parameter list (p. 34) | the list ends with a comma after "Out" and says "Location" | eight commands as printed; the list may be cut short; unverified |
| Note and [PB](13-glossary.md#pitch-bend-pb) tables | fields are named "Parameter (controller)" and "Value"; pitch bend has no controller number | note number and velocity for Note; the PB meaning is unknown; unverified |
| [PC](13-glossary.md#program-change-pc) tables | the parameter is named "bank number" | probably the program number; unverified |
| ZAQ mode intro | "hold EDIT/GLOBAL (59) while moving any encoder adjusts all [steps](13-glossary.md#step) until max or min" | Verified on firmware 1.0.3: pressing EDIT (B59) opens the [ZAQ Global page](13-glossary.md#zaq-global-page) and the key flashes. It does not edit steps. Holding a parameter button (tested: LENGTH, B9) and turning one knob one notch changed all 32 steps. One notch back restored them. The max or min behaviour was not seen |
| Transpose enable list | "1-4 … 13-16" | Verified on firmware 1.0.3: the list has 31 values: OFF, CH 1 to CH 16, [TRACK](13-glossary.md#track), then the windows 1-4, 2-5 and so on up to 13-16. The windows overlap |
| MIDI out list (E41) | the full list is not shown | Verified on firmware 1.0.3 in USB mode: E41 has three values, U, AB IN and IN. The value IN is the routing for a transposing track. The full list needs MIXED |
| MIDI through | "[SELECT encoder](13-glossary.md#select-encoder-sel) (58) switches Source to Destination" | Source set with E28: OFF, MIDI, USB (verified). In our test, turning E28 after the SEL push still changed the source. The destination list is not read. The manual says the select knob sets it |
| Encoder modes REL1, REL3 | REL1 sends "minimum for CCW, maximum for CW". REL3 sends 1 for CCW and 65 for CW | Verified on firmware 1.0.3, clockwise side only: REL1 sends `01` per click, REL2 sends `41`, REL3 sends `01`. The counter-clockwise side is untested |
| Pattern change channel (E33) | the manual calls E33 "trigger enable" | Verified on firmware 1.0.3: the [display](13-glossary.md#display-disp) shows "PAT.N CH" with the value OFF. It is the same setting as pattern change channel in Global Settings (B13) |

Procedures that depend on a row in this table are unconfirmed until someone tests them on a unit. Record test results in the row and in the [changelog](../../CHANGELOG.md).

<!-- file: docs/manual/13-glossary.md -->

# 13. Glossary

Each term has one meaning in this manual. Use the term, not a synonym. The first use of a term in each chapter links to its entry.

## Unit and panel

### ZAQ mode

The mode in which the unit is a step sequencer. Button B1 is pink. The panel also prints ZAQ and ZQR. Tap B1 to change mode.

### CTRL mode

The mode in which the unit is a MIDI controller. Button B1 is amber.

### Control ID

The fixed name of one control in this manual, such as B5, E25 or J70. The IDs follow the callout numbers of the official manual.

### Callout

A number in the panel drawing of the official manual. It points to one control. The control ID uses it.

### Encoder

A knob with a push switch and a ring of LEDs. The unit has 32 encoders (E25 to E56). Turn an encoder to change a value. Push it to switch or confirm.

### Ring LED

The ring of LEDs around an encoder. It shows a value, a note or the playhead.

### Display (DISP)

The screen of the unit. It shows the parameter and its value.

### Select encoder (SEL)

The large encoder near the display. Turn it to pick a value. Push it to confirm.

### Footswitch

A pedal on jack J74 or J75. Global Settings sets what it does.

## Sequencer

### Track

One of four independent lines of the sequencer. Buttons B21 to B24 select it. Each track has its own MIDI port and channel.

### Step

One of 32 positions in a track. Step k is encoder E(24+k).

### Pattern

The notes and settings of all four tracks, kept together. A pattern is stored in a slot. The official manual also uses the word sequence for this. This manual uses pattern.

### Page

A group of 16 slots. There are 12 pages. Buttons B63 and B64 change the page.

### Slot

One of the 16 places on a page that can hold a pattern. Buttons B5 to B20 select it.

### Chord

Several notes played from one step. Button B13 sets the chord type of each step. It works on MIDI output only.

### Drum track

A track in Drum mode. Buttons B5 to B20 then select 16 drum voices.

### Drum voice

One of the 16 sounds of a drum track. Each voice has its own note.

### Playhead

The step that plays now. The last three LEDs of the ring show it.

### Mixer

The view in which you mute tracks and drum voices. Press B66 while the sequencer is stopped.

### Real-time record

The mode in which the unit records notes while the pattern plays. Press B65 to start it.

### Note repeat

The function that repeats a note at a set rate. Hold B64 and turn an encoder to set the rate.

### Wave generator

A source of values for the parameter lanes, such as pitch and velocity. Button B12 controls it. The panel prints WAVE GEN.

### Scale

A set of allowed notes. The unit bends the notes to the scale at playback. The stored notes do not change.

### Shuffle

A delay of the even steps or the odd steps. Button B19 sets it.

### Quantize

The function that moves recorded notes to the nearest step grid.

### Transpose

The function that shifts the notes of a track when the unit receives MIDI notes.

### Control lane

A row of values that sends a MIDI control change on each step. Buttons B10 and B11 set the lanes alpha and beta.

## Controller

### Preset

A saved set of controller assignments. The unit holds 64 presets. The editor files also call a sequencer pattern a preset.

### Learn

The mode in which the unit copies an assignment from an incoming MIDI message. Hold B62 and use a control.

### Permanent store

The extra step that keeps a pattern or a preset after power-off. Hold SEL and press B61. Without it, the unit loses the data at power-off.

### Control change (CC)

A MIDI message with a controller number from 0 to 127 and a value.

### Program change (PC)

A MIDI message that selects a program or sound on another device.

### NRPN

A MIDI message type that addresses a parameter by a 14-bit number. The name means non-registered parameter number.

### Pitch bend (PB)

A MIDI message with a 14-bit value, made for a pitch wheel.

### Aftertouch (AT)

A MIDI message that sends the pressure on a key after the key press.

### MMC

MIDI machine control. These messages start, stop and wind a recorder. The official manual calls them MIDI machine code.

## Sync, ports and settings

### BPM

Beats per minute. The unit accepts 30 to 300 with its internal clock.

### Clock source

The origin of the tempo: Internal, MIDI, USB or Sync. Knob E26 on the ZAQ Global page sets it.

### Operation mode

The setting that decides which ports work: USB, STDL or MIXED. Global Settings button B7 sets it.

### ppqn

Pulses per quarter note. The sync jacks use it. ZAQ Settings sets the value.

### MIDI thru

The function that forwards incoming MIDI to an output.

### SysEx

System exclusive. A MIDI message that starts with F0 and ends with F7. The unit uses SysEx for backups.

### DIN MIDI

The 5-pin MIDI sockets J71 to J73.

### USB-MIDI

MIDI over the USB-C port J70.

### CV

Control voltage. The unit has four CV outputs with 1 volt per octave.

### Gate

A voltage that is on while a note plays. The level is 5 V or 10 V.

### Firmware

The software inside the unit. Global Settings button B11 shows its version.

### Global Settings

The menu for settings of the whole unit. Hold B1 for three seconds to open it.

### ZAQ Settings

The menu for sync and gate settings of the sequencer. Hold B59 and press B61 in ZAQ mode.

### CTRL Settings

The menu for settings of the controller. Hold B59 and press B61 in CTRL mode.

### ZAQ Global page

The page of sequencer settings on the encoders. Press B59 in ZAQ mode.

### Factory restore

The function that sets the unit back to its factory state. Global Settings button B12 starts it.

### Control Tribe

The editor program from the maker of the unit. It saves and loads the memory of the unit.

---

<!-- file: docs/manual/14-generated-tables-and-indexes.md -->

# 14. Generated tables and indexes

A tool writes every table in this chapter from the device data. Do not edit a table by hand. To change a table, change the data in `data/devices/bcr32/` and run `npm run gen:tables`.

The three indexes of the manual are:

- **By control:** [Index by control](#index-by-control).
- **By function:** [Index by function](#index-by-function).
- **By task:** [chapter 10](10-quick-lookup-how-do-i.md). A person writes it, because the device data holds no tasks.

## Control tables by mode

Each table lists the functions of one mode. The Source column shows where the fact comes from.

### ZAQ (sequencer)

### CTRL (controller)

<!-- gen:functions mode=ctrl -->

| Controls | Function | Action | Values | Default | MIDI seen (firmware 1.0.3) | Source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `B1` | Go to ZAQ mode | `tap B1` | — | — | — | manual |
| `B5`–`B24`, `E25`–`E56`, `B65`–`B68` | Send the assigned MIDI message | — | — | — | ch 1: CC 5, 7, 9, 12, 14–18, 40–42, 44–53, 65–80, 85, 87–90, 97–98 | manual |

<!-- file: docs/manual/15-known-issues.md -->

# 15. Known issues

This chapter lists faults and limits of the unit and of its editor software. It is not the list of errors in the official manual. That list is [chapter 12](12-source-errors-and-gaps.md).

## How to read the register

- **Own test:** we saw it on our own unit. The row names the [firmware](13-glossary.md#firmware) version.
- **User report:** a person wrote it on a public [page](13-glossary.md#page). We did not test it. We name no person, only the page and the date.
- **Firmware:** the version that the source states. "Not stated" means the source gives none.
- **Newest firmware named:** 1.0.3. We found no release notes and no newer version.

| Status | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Open | seen, and no fix or cause is known |
| Unconfirmed | one report, or reports that disagree; we did not reproduce it |
| Limit | the unit or the software does not offer the function |
| Workaround | a reported [step](13-glossary.md#step) avoids the fault |
| Resolved | a source says the fault is fixed |

## Register

| ID | Symptom | Firmware | Source | Date | Reliability | Status | Workaround |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| K1 | The panel export (STORE, hold [SEL](13-glossary.md#select-encoder-sel), push the knob printed 1 (E25), then the knob printed 5 (E29)) shows "export mode". The unit then sends nothing on USB | 1.0.3 | own test, [findings](../reference/capture-findings.md#backup-exports-step-42) | 2026-11-11 | own test | Open | Export with the vendor editor |
| K2 | B5 sent no message in the first test run and [CC](13-glossary.md#control-change-cc) 65 in the second. The cause is unknown | 1.0.3 | own test, [findings](../reference/capture-findings.md#midi-facts) | 2026-11-11 | own test | Open | none |
| K3 | A push of the knob printed 1 (E25) sent no message. The push may be unassigned, or it needs a firmer push | 1.0.3 | own test, [findings](../reference/capture-findings.md#midi-facts) | 2026-11-11 | own test | Open | none |
| K4 | Turning two or more [encoders](13-glossary.md#encoder) at the same time can make the unit fall behind. One report adds a "Controller Overload" message on the [display](13-glossary.md#display-disp), once | not stated | Thomann reviews; Elektronauts thread, page 11 | 2026-10-30, 2026-11-07 | community, multiple | Unconfirmed | none reported |
| K5 | The LED display lags while the sequencer runs | not stated | Elektronauts thread, page 11 | 2026-10-04 | community, single | Unconfirmed | none reported |
| K6 | The computer or the editor does not find the unit. On Windows 11 one reviewer fixed this with the editor menu Help, Repair Driver | not stated | Elektronauts thread, page 10; Thomann reviews | 2026-09-25, 2026-09-29 | community, multiple | Workaround | Repair Driver in the editor, as one reviewer reports |
| K7 | The editor cannot copy and paste the settings of a single knob | 1.0.3 | Elektronauts thread, page 12 | 2026-11-09 | community, single | Unconfirmed | none |
| K8 | The editor has no tool for note [patterns](13-glossary.md#pattern), pitches or velocities. One reviewer could not tell how patterns are saved | not stated | Thomann reviews | 2026-10-30 | community, single | Limit | none; see the [web UI references](../project/web-ui-references.md) for a community tool |
| K9 | [SysEx](13-glossary.md#sysex) input works only when the user copies BCR2000 messages to the unit, says one reviewer. A second reviewer says SysEx in and out work | not stated | Thomann reviews | 2026-09-25, 2026-10-30 | community, multiple, conflicting | Unconfirmed | none |
| K10 | Reports of play in the encoders disagree. One reviewer reports about 1.5 mm each way. Another finds no play | not stated | Elektronauts thread, page 10; Thomann reviews | 2026-09-27, 2026-10-30 | community, multiple, conflicting | Unconfirmed | none |
| K11 | The manual was not online at launch | not stated | Elektronauts thread, page 10; Thomann reviews | 2026-09-25 to 2026-09-28 | community, multiple | Resolved | The manual Rev1 was posted 2026-09-28 |
| K12 | Reviewers call the manual hard to follow. One example is the MIDI channel set-up in three sections | not stated | Thomann reviews | 2026-10-30 | retailer reviews, multiple | Unconfirmed | Use this manual and chapter 12 |
| K13 | The press article says the launch firmware was weak. One reviewer says later updates fixed most faults and added encoder acceleration. No source names the faults | not stated | Synth Anatomy article; Thomann reviews | 2026-10-30, 2026-09-25 | press and retailer review | Unconfirmed | Update the firmware with the vendor editor |
| K14 | The QR code on the box led to a missing page. No source says that it was fixed | not stated | Elektronauts thread, page 10; Thomann reviews | 2026-09-25 to 2026-09-27 | community, multiple | Unconfirmed | Use the manual from the vendor product page |
| K15 | The keys at the right of the panel (EDIT, EXIT, STORE, LD/LRN, TAP DELETE, TAP WRITE, INST SEL, [MIXER](13-glossary.md#mixer), reset, play/stop) and the [track](13-glossary.md#track) keys T1 to T4 send no message in [CTRL mode](13-glossary.md#ctrl-mode). No `$button` number is known for them | 1.0.3 | own test, [MIDI implementation](16-midi-implementation.md) | 2026-11-13 | own test, repeated | Open | They work as menu keys. [ZAQ mode](13-glossary.md#zaq-mode) and the ZAQ port are untested |

## Claims that we could not confirm

We opened the sources again on 2026-11-11. These claims do not stand:

- **Fast-cut lag of about 50 ms:** the post says "faders", and the BCR32 has none. The thread also discusses another controller.
- **No [DIN MIDI](13-glossary.md#din-midi) output routing:** the claim came from a search snippet. We found no page.
- **Windows update fault:** we found no source for a named Windows update.
- **Unprinted functions under the knobs:** we did not find the post again.

## Sources

| Source | Address |
| --- | --- |
| Elektronauts thread, pages 10 to 12 | `https://www.elektronauts.com/t/behringer-bcr32/145603` |
| Thomann product and reviews page | `https://www.thomann.de/be/behringer_bcr32.htm` |
| Synth Anatomy article | `https://synthanatomy.com/2026/10/behringer-bcr32-bcr2000-midi-controller-comeback-with-built-in-zaquencer.html` |
| Vendor product page | `https://www.behringer.com/en/products/0715-AAW` |

User reports can be wrong. A row in "Unconfirmed" needs a test on a unit before anyone relies on it. Report a new issue with the correction issue template.

<!-- file: docs/manual/16-midi-implementation.md -->

# MIDI implementation

No official MIDI chart exists for the BCR32. Every row in this chapter comes from a test on one unit with [firmware](13-glossary.md#firmware) 1.0.3. Nothing here is a promise for other firmware.

> **Note:** All results are from the USB ports. The DIN ports are untested, because no [DIN MIDI](13-glossary.md#din-midi) interface was available.

## 16.1 Ports

The unit shows two USB MIDI ports to the computer.

| Port | Use |
| --- | --- |
| BCR-32 CTRL | The controller part. The unit sends controller messages from here. |
| BCR-32 ZAQ | The sequencer part. The unit sends nothing here in the tests so far. |

The USB vendor ID is 1397. The product ID is 12CF in normal mode. See `data/devices/bcr32/midi.json` for the full record.

## 16.2 What the unit sends

In [CTRL mode](13-glossary.md#ctrl-mode) the unit sends the messages of the active [preset](13-glossary.md#preset). Each control sends the message that the preset assigns to it.

The table below lists every message seen. Each row names the controls, the preset it came from and how sure we are.

| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

| `ctrl-cc98` | BCR-32 CTRL | ctrl | `E26` | cc | 1 | 98 | 1, 2 | likely |
| `ctrl-preset-name` | BCR-32 CTRL | ctrl | — | sysex | — | — | — | — |
| `ctrl.p1.b5` | BCR-32 CTRL | ctrl | `B5` | cc | 1 | 65 | 127 | proven |
| `ctrl.p1.b6` | BCR-32 CTRL | ctrl | `B6` | cc | 1 | 66 | 127 | proven |

- **Proven:** the control was pressed on its own and the message was logged.
- **Likely:** the message matches the stored assignment, but the action time is not known.
- **Silent controls:** buttons B21 to B24 and B65 to B68 sent nothing on any port. The [encoders](13-glossary.md#encoder) E30, E31 and E38 are unassigned in preset 4.
- **Preset switch:** the unit changed its active preset between two runs. The cause is not proven.

## 16.3 What the unit did not do

A test with no message or no effect is a result. These tests found nothing to log.

<!-- gen:midi-silences -->

| ID | Port | Mode | Action | Result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `idle` | — | zaq | Leave the unit idle with both ports open. | No clock, no active sensing and no other message. |
| `zaq-keyboard` | — | zaq-record | Press the virtual keyboard buttons in NOTE mode. | Nothing on either port. |
| `zaq-transport` | — | zaq | Press PLAY/STOP (B68) to start, then to stop. | Nothing on either port. B68 was solid red while the sequencer ran. |
| `ctrl-first-listen` | BCR-32 CTRL | ctrl | Turn encoder 1 once and press button 1 once, before the routing was read. | Nothing on USB. |
| `ctrl-silent-track-buttons` | BCR-32 CTRL | ctrl | Press B21, B22, B23 and B24 once each, in presets 1 and 4. | Nothing on any port, in four runs. |
| `ctrl-silent-right-buttons` | BCR-32 CTRL | ctrl | Press B65, B66, B67 and B68 once each. | Nothing on any port, in four runs. |
| `ctrl-silent-unassigned-knobs` | BCR-32 CTRL | ctrl | Turn E30, E31 and E38 (knobs printed 6, 7 and 14) both ways. | Nothing. The three knobs have no lit LED ring. |
| `ctrl-silent-preset-buttons` | BCR-32 CTRL | ctrl | Press B64, then B63. | Nothing on any port. |
| `ctrl-pushes` | BCR-32 CTRL | ctrl | Push each knob E25 to E56 once, without turning it. | 28 of 32 pushes sent nothing. Four pushes sent a message that is not explained. |
| `inbound-identity-ctrl` | BCR-32 CTRL | zaq | Send the identity request F0 7E 7F 06 01 F7 to the CTRL port. | No reply and no change on the unit. |
| `inbound-identity-zaq` | BCR-32 ZAQ | zaq | Send the identity request F0 7E 7F 06 01 F7 to the ZAQ port. | No reply and no change on the unit. |
| `inbound-start-stop` | BCR-32 ZAQ | zaq | Send start (FA), then 3 seconds later stop (FC), to the ZAQ port. | No reply. PLAY/STOP did not light. The unit stayed with the internal clock source. |
| `inbound-note` | BCR-32 ZAQ | zaq | Send note on (channel 1, note 60, velocity 100), then note off, to the ZAQ port. | No reply and no change. Transpose was Off. |
| `inbound-cc-pc` | BCR-32 ZAQ | zaq | Send controller change 1 value 64, then program change 2, on channel 1 to the ZAQ port. | No reply. The pattern did not change. Pattern change channel (B13) was Off. |

<!-- gen:end -->

> **Warning:** The unit sends no reply when it ignores a message. A silent result does not prove that the unit did nothing. It proves only that the output, the [display](13-glossary.md#display-disp) and the LEDs did not change.

## 16.4 What the unit accepts

Five tests sent standard messages to the unit with the settings as found. None had an effect. Section 16.3 lists them.

| Message | Needs, probably | Tested |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Start and stop | USB [clock source](13-glossary.md#clock-source) | no |
| Notes as [transpose](13-glossary.md#transpose) | Transpose on (E32) | no |
| [Program change](13-glossary.md#program-change-pc) as [pattern](13-glossary.md#pattern) switch | Pattern change channel (B13) on | no |
| Identity request | A device ID that matches | no |

Each "needs" entry is a guess from the settings. A test of each needs a setting change on the unit. That test needs a fresh backup check first. See the [unit safety protocol](../project/unit-safety.md).

## 16.5 Editor and dump format

[Control Tribe](13-glossary.md#control-tribe) reads controller presets as text, one line per [SysEx](13-glossary.md#sysex) message. It also reads the sequencer state when you connect and when you select a sequencer preset. The [findings page](../reference/capture-findings.md#editor-protocol-step-45) has the message layout.

The backup `.syx` files use another layout. The [findings page](../reference/capture-findings.md#sysex-dump-structure-step-46) describes it. The check value at the end of each [slot](13-glossary.md#slot) is a CRC-32, and the dump rules are solved. See the [SysEx dump format](../reference/sysex-dump-format.md). Do not edit a dump file without a backup.

## 16.6 How to extend this chapter

1. Test on the unit with `midi-capture`. Give the printed number and the ID of every control.
2. Add the result to `data/devices/bcr32/midi.json` with the firmware version.
3. Run `npm run gen:tables`. The tables above and the MIDI column in chapter 14 update.

## 16.7 Message forms verified in test presets

Verified on firmware 1.0.3 on 2026-11-13, USB port `BCR-32 CTRL`, with crafted test presets. The tables in 16.2 hold the first factory presets. This table holds the message forms.

| Setting | What the unit sends |
| --- | --- |
| [CC](13-glossary.md#control-change-cc) absolute | The CC value. The first click gives 1 |
| CC relative-1, relative-2, relative-3 | `01`, `41` and `01` per click clockwise |
| CC absolute 14 bit | CC n (high part), then CC n+32 (low part) |
| [NRPN](13-glossary.md#nrpn) | CC 99 (high), CC 98 (low), then CC 6 (data). Inc/dec sends CC 96 with `01` per click |
| GS/XG cutoff and resonance | NRPN `01:20` and `01:21` |
| GS/XG volume and panorama | Plain CC 7 and CC 10 |
| Encoder [AT](13-glossary.md#aftertouch-at), all notes | Channel pressure (`0xD0`) |
| Encoder AT, one note | Poly pressure (`0xA0`) |
| [Pitch bend](13-glossary.md#pitch-bend-pb) | `0xE0` and `0xE1` for channels 1 and 2 |
| Button toggle off | The value on press, the minimum on release |
| Button toggle on | The value on press only |
| Button PC | A program change with the number as written. The bank sends CC 0 only. CC 32 is never sent |
| [MMC](13-glossary.md#mmc) | `F0 7F <device> 06 <command> F7`. Locate has the longer form with the time bytes |

**Knob pushes:** The push of the knobs printed 1 to 12 (E25 to E36) is `$button` 17 to 28 in the preset text. Each push sent the message that the preset assigns to it. The pushes in 16.3 sent nothing because they had no assignment in those presets. See the [BCL preset text format](../reference/bcl-preset-text-format.md).

**Rejected by the unit:** an encoder AT line with a mode word, a CC with inc/dec, and the LED words `pan/off`, `spread/off` and `qual/off`.
